Foreword
Recent geopolitical upheavals and rapid technological
development require particularly well-considered decisions in
corporate management; for example, today the ability to make
long-term investment decisions in uncertain circumstances has
become a critical factor for success. We need to stay alert, not only
to respond to sudden challenges, but to systematically shape the
future of the Baltic energy sector. Therefore, the motto for the
Group’s development for the past year has been strategic growth
and energy independence.
In a sense, this year has been a historic turning point: for the first
time, almost half of the electricity sold by Latvenergo was
marketed outside Latvia’s borders, compared with one third a year
earlier.
At the beginning of last year, the Baltic states implemented one of
the most significant projects in the history of independent Latvia:
the successful disconnection from the energy system of the
former Soviet western region (BRELL) and synchronisation with the
European grid via Poland. This step not only improves the region’s
energy security, but also eliminates any possibility of manipulative
disruption by Russia.
With this synchronisation, the Baltic balancing capacity market
was established, in which Latvenergo participates effectively with
the capacities of CHPP-2 and hydroelectric power plants. Another
major development in the market is the transition of the Nord Pool
exchange to 15-minute market time units. These changes make it
possible to adapt better to the variability of solar and wind power,
to balance consumption more accurately with generation from
renewables, and, in future, to offer customers more attractive
prices thanks to more efficient integration of green energy.
Although we began developing renewable resource capacities
later than our neighbouring countries, this has allowed us to gain

Regulatory framework                      Consolidated annual report has been prepared in accordance with:
                                            • Law on Annual Statements and Consolidated Annual Statements
                                            • International Financial Reporting Standards as adopted by the European Union (IFRS)
                                            • Law on Governance of Capital Shares of a Public Person and Capital Companies
                                            • Financial Instruments Market Law
                                            • Sustainability Information Disclosure Law
                                            • European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772
                                            • Taxonomy Regulation (EU) 2020/852
Scope of the report                       The report discloses information about Latvenergo Group (see the section About the Group).

Content of the report                     The report discloses information about the topics and indicators that are material for the operations and sustainability of the Group.
                                          ESRS 2 General Information are fully covered, and, based on the double materiality assessment – 8 ESRS topical standards.
                                          Financial Statements include Statement of Financial Position as at 31 December 2025 and Statement of Profit or Loss, Statement of Comprehensive Income,
                                          Statement of Changes in Equity, Statement of Cash Flows for the year ended 31 December 2025, as well as Notes to the Financial Statements including
                                          material accounting policy information.

Approval of the report                    The Annual Report is signed electronically by the Management Board of Latvenergo AS, reviewed by the Supervisory Board and approved by the
                                          Shareholder.

Independent auditors’ reports             Independent auditors' assurance report on the sustainability statement and independent auditors' report on the financial statements has been prepared by
                                          Ernst & Young Baltic SIA.

                                            • on the Nasdaq Baltic website www.nasdaqbaltic.com (in Latvian and English)
                                            • on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange website www.luxse.com (in English)
                                            • in the Central Storage of Regulated Information https://csri.investinfo.lv (in Latvian and English)

Contact information                       Please send any questions or suggestions to: sustainability@latvenergo.lv.

=== pdf p.7 ===
About the Group
Latvenergo Group is one of the largest providers of energy supply
services in the Baltics, operating in:
 • electricity and thermal energy generation and trade
 • natural gas trade
 • trade in products and services                related     to   electricity
   consumption and energy efficiency
 • electricity distribution
The Group’s operations have been organised into two operating
segments. One segment covers generation and trade, while the
other comprises the distribution of electricity. For more information,
see the section Operating Segments.
The Group comprises the parent company Latvenergo AS, with
decisive influence, and a set of subsidiaries. All shares of
Latvenergo AS are owned by the Republic of Latvia, and they are
held by the Ministry of Economics of the Republic of Latvia.
Information about the participating interests in the subsidiaries and
their locations is disclosed in Notes 1 and 16 of the Financial
Statements.

=== pdf p.12 ===
HPPs
Kegums, Plavinas and Riga HPPs are the largest hydropower
plants in the country and provide a high share of renewable energy
not only in the Group, but also in Latvia as a whole. Their ability to
generate electricity depends on the water inflow in the Daugava
River. During the spring flooding, it is possible to cover the demand
for electricity of all Latvenergo Group’s customers and trade the
excess on the Nord Pool exchange. Outside the flood season, the
Daugava HPPs can accumulate water in short term and adjust
generation of electricity when the demand and prices on the
exchange are higher. Electricity is also generated at the Aiviekste
HPP, which is one of the first hydropower plants in Latvia.

SPPs and WPPs                                                         Principles for developing WPPs
Latvenergo Group is actively continuing its work on expanding
generation capacity from renewable energy sources, which will
contribute to achieving national climate goals and strengthening
energy security. The focus is on the development of WPPs and
SPPs.
At the end of 2025, the Group’s newly installed renewable energy
capacities in the Baltics reached 498 MW – 22 solar parks with an
installed capacity of 353 MW and 3 wind parks with an installed
capacity of 145 MW. The largest renewable energy source parks
built are the Telšiai WPP in Lithuania (124 MW), the Kiškėnai SPP
in Lithuania (91 MW) and the Klaipeda SPP in Lithuania (78 MW).
Projects with a total capacity of 646 MW are currently under
construction, of which 336 MW are solar projects and 310 MW are
wind projects. The largest renewable energy projects are the
Aizpute solar park in Latvia (265 MW), the Pienava wind park in
Latvia (147 MW), and the Laflora Energy wind park in Latvia (109
MW). At the time of the report’s publication, construction of the
Aizpute solar park has been completed and the facility has started
generating electricity. Gradual commissioning of the solar and
wind parks currently under construction is expected between
2026 and 2027. After the construction of the new renewable
energy assets, the Group’s annual electricity generation is
expected to increase by approximately 2.2 TWh.                        For more information on the development of wind farms and wind
Alongside the new RES capacities, BESS projects are also being        energy use, visit the Latvenergo website.

10.6 MW / 21.9 MWh were built. As of the report’s date of approval,
six BESS projects with a total capacity of 183.4 MW / 428.6 MWh
are in the development stage.

=== pdf p.15 ===
Trade
Latvenergo Group is one of the largest electricity traders in the Baltic states; it offers electricity and
natural gas, as well as an extensive range of related products and services under the Elektrum brand.
                                                                                                                 Elektrum in the Baltic electricity market
Electricity
At the end of 2025, Latvenergo Group had more than 914 thousand customers in the Baltic states,
including more than 306 thousand customers outside Latvia. Of the total number of electricity
customers, 96 % are household customers and 4 % are business customers. The market share of
Latvenergo Group in the electricity market of the Baltic states was about 22%, while its share in the
Latvian electricity market was around 46%.

Natural gas
The number of natural gas customers in the Baltic states at the end of 2025 exceeded 76 thousand.
Of the total number of natural gas customers, 96% are household customers and 4% are business
customers. The market share of Latvenergo Group in the natural gas market of the Baltic states was
about 7%, while its share in the Latvian natural gas market was around 22%.

Charging network for electric cars
By the end of 2025, the number of charging ports installed at Elektrum Drive charging stations had
increased to 1,107. The Elektrum Drive app can also be used to charge vehicles on the e-mobi network
in Latvia and at LIDL charging stations in Lithuania and Estonia, with a total of 1,590 charging ports
available to Elektrum Drive app customers across the Baltic states.
Elektrum Drive conducts public awareness and education activities in the field of electric vehicles and
charging infrastructure, providing free consultations, organizing informational events, and preparing
and distributing publications and explanatory materials. The Elektrum Drive electric vehicle test catalog
offers data on the efficiency of more than 80 electric vehicles available for purchase in Latvia. This
information supports prospective electric vehicle owners in evaluating the efficiency of electric
vehicles available on the market.

Other products
The Latvenergo Group offers a range of insurance services to its customers, including products such
as protection against power supply disruptions and damage to electrical appliances (with emergency
assistance from professional electricians, plumbers, carpenters, and locksmiths), insurance covering
fire risks related to electrical installations and devices, and financial support for electricity and gas bill
payments in the event of unforeseen circumstances (such as prolonged incapacity to work due to
health issues or unemployment), and insurance for heating equipment. The Elektrum Insured customer
portfolio in the Baltic states reached almost 174 thousand customers.

Electricity market and market players
                                        The price of electricity on the bills of end-users in Latvia consists
                                        of:
                                         • the price of electricity, which includes generation and trading
                                           costs
                                         • charges for transmission and distribution system services
                                           provided by Augstspriegumu tīkls AS and Sadales tīkls AS
                                         • value-added tax
                                        Customers can calculate the breakdown of their electricity bills
                                        according to electricity consumption and products they choose
                                        using the Elektrum calculator.


                                        In Latvia, a state-established support mechanism has been
                                        introduced for electricity producers generating electricity in
                                        cogeneration plants or from renewable energy sources. It is
                                        implemented as electricity mandatory procurement (MP) or
                                        guaranteed payments for the electrical capacity installed at
                                        cogeneration plants. Until 2012, the right to sell electricity
                                        generated within MP or receive guaranteed payments for the
                                        installed electrical capacity at cogeneration plants was granted by
                                        the Ministry of Economics. Costs related to MP are covered by the
                                        state budget. A portion of the dividends of Latvenergo AS is
                                        allocated to cover MP costs. In compliance with the Electricity
                                        Market Law, the functions of the public trader in Latvia are
                                        performed by Enerģijas publiskais tirgotājs SIA. More information
                                        about MP can be found on the website of Enerģijas publiskais
                                        tirgotājs SIA.

=== pdf p.18 ===
Group Strategy
  Overall strategic goal of Latvenergo Group approved by the Cabinet of
  Ministers of the Republic of Latvia
  To promote the competitiveness and growth of a climate-neutral Latvia and
  increase the value of Latvenergo Group in the Baltic market and beyond by
  developing and providing goods and services in the energy and related
  business value chains in a sustainable, innovative and economically sound
  manner and by efficiently managing strategically important resources and
  infrastructure.


The Medium-term Operational Strategy of Latvenergo Group for 2022–2026 aims
to achieve a high share of RES in electricity generation by significantly
complementing existing generation capacity with solar and wind power plants.
Following nearly a decade focused on cost optimisation and operational efficiency,
these years have marked a shift toward rapid growth and substantial investment,
resulting in a significant increase in RES generation capacities. This will help to
prevent future electricity price hikes and strengthen the energy independence of
Latvia and the Baltic region as a whole.
The Group’s strategy has been developed in accordance with the requirements of
the Law on Governance of Capital Shares of a Public Person and Capital Companies
and the Guidelines for the Development of Medium-Term Operational Strategies for
State Capital Companies approved by the Cross-Sectoral Coordination Centre 1 of
the Republic of Latvia with consideration of the guidelines of the Organisation for
Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).
The strategic priorities of the Group correspond to the overall strategic goal set by
the Cabinet of Ministers (CM) of the Republic of Latvia, and they are further detailed
in the operational and financial targets.
  • Operational targets – set out the strategic development directions of Latvenergo
    Group and the main activities to achieve these targets, as well as provide a
    trajectory for the development of the Group towards the indicative targets for
    2030 and beyond
  • Financial targets – ambitious but realistic targets that can ensure the sustainable
    development of the company
As the current strategy implementation period draws to a close, the development
of the next medium-term operational strategy for Latvenergo Group has
commenced, involving analysis of the external and internal environment and an
assessment of future development opportunities.




1 From 1 March 2023, the functions of the Cross-Sectoral Coordination Centre have been transferred to the
State Chancellery.

=== pdf p.20 ===
Implementation of the Group’s operational targets in 2025                                                     RES capacity development

Generation target:
to expand and diversify the generation portfolio with green technologies

The target is to grow the RES generation portfolio, focusing on WPPs and SPPs, to increase the value
of HPPs’ assets, ensuring their safe operation in the long term, and to ensure the stable, efficient and
economically sound operation of CHPPs in the long term.

The year 2025 was a year of significant investment, with EUR 792 million invested, which is 49% more
than in the previous year. More than two-thirds of the investments, or EUR 548 million, were allocated
to new wind and solar generation capacities. At the end of the reporting year, newly constructed RES
capacities in the Baltics already totalled 498 MW, while solar and wind power plants under
development had a combined capacity of 646 MW. Thus, the total approved portfolio of new RES
projects amounted to 1,144 MW. Demonstrating its strategic commitment to being the leading
renewable energy company in the Baltic states, the Group is also investing in BESS technologies, with
plans to install 250 MW of capacity and 500 MWh of storage by 2030. In the reporting year, two BESS
projects were constructed with a total capacity of 10.6 MW and an installed storage capacity of
21.9 MWh. At the time of publication of the report, six BESS projects are under development with a
total capacity of 183.4 MW and a planned storage capacity of 428.6 MWh. For information on the
development of solar and wind parks, see the section Investments under Results.
Regarding Daugava HPP hydro unit refurbishment, reconstruction work on the Plavinas HPP hydro unit
is ongoing, and significant efforts have been made to attract a cooperation partner for the
reconstruction of two Kegums HPP hydro units. At Riga HPP, the replacement of primary equipment
has been completed, including the delivery of two new 250 MVA step-up transformers. At the same
time, a unified technical management system project for the Daugava HPPs has been developed and
installation work has commenced. In addition, a range of hydro unit control logic renewal,
enhancement and calibration work has been carried out, enabling the Daugava HPP hydro units to
qualify for the provision of technically feasible balancing ancillary services (mFRR, aFRR and FCR).          RES capacities portfolio   Geolocation of newly constructed RES capacities
Several projects are being implemented to improve the operational efficiency of CHPPs, in order to
increase the flexibility of electricity generation and the efficiency of heat production processes, as well
as to reduce energy resource consumption. In 2025, a heat network heat carrier cooling system was
commissioned at CHPP-1 and a BESS was installed, significantly improving the CHPP generation
capacity portfolio. The cogeneration units of CHPP-2, together with technically feasible CHPP-1
equipment, have been qualified for the transmission system operator’s balancing ancillary services,
thereby enhancing the security of the energy supply in the Baltics. Furthermore, in the reporting year,
a project for the construction of electrode boilers was launched at the CHPP-2 site, in order to expand
the range of balancing services offered by the CHPP and to ensure competitive heat production during
periods of low electricity prices.

=== pdf p.22 ===
Distribution target:
to ensure a sustainable and economically viable distribution service and to improve the security
and quality of the electricity supply                                                                      SAIFI

The target is to improve the quality and reliability of the electricity supply in a planned and cost-
effective manner, as well as to develop a two-way grid appropriate for microgeneration and to
implement digital transformation and efficiency measures.

The main indicators characterising the quality of the electricity supply are the system average
interruption frequency index (SAIFI) and the duration in minutes (SAIDI). Year-on-year improvements
in both indicators are driven by targeted investments in the maintenance, reconstruction and
modernisation of distribution electricity networks. The share of weather-resistant electricity networks
(underground cables, suspended cables, insulated overhead lines) is approaching 70%, and in 2025,
Sadales tīkls AS recorded the lowest ever number of faults in the electricity network – 11 thousand
faults (excluding natural disasters), which is almost three times lower than a decade ago. Over the past
five years (2020–2025), excluding mass fault situations, SAIFI has decreased by 26% and SAIDI has
decreased by 39%.
Another important investment objective is to strengthen the distribution network’s readiness for
increasing loads and RES integration. At the end of 2025, the number of electricity producers of various
capacities connected to the distribution system reached 26.7 thousand (including solar and wind
generators, as well as SPPs combined with BESS, HPPs, natural gas or biogas cogeneration plants,
etc.), with a total generation capacity of 1.19 GW (at the end of 2024, approximately 24.7 thousand
electricity producers of various capacities were connected to the distribution system, with a total        SAIDI
generation capacity exceeding 910 MW). Solar energy is playing an increasingly important role in the
overall electricity balance, and in the reporting year, approximately 600 GWh of electricity generated
from solar energy was delivered to the grid via the distribution system, accounting for about 10% of
the total electricity distributed in the system, which is 1.5 times more than in 2024.
Sadales tīkls AS is currently the only electricity distribution operator in the Baltics that uses and
develops data-driven artificial intelligence solutions for assessing the condition of power lines and
detecting defects, carrying out inspections with drones. In 2025, power lines with a total length of
3,100 km were inspected in this way and 110 potentially dangerous defects were identified, allowing
them to be rectified in a timely manner. Since 2023, the “Step” electricity market data exchange
platform has been available to participants in the Latvian electricity market. It is an information
technology system designed to provide standardised and centralised preparation, storage and
exchange of electricity market data between market participants and system operators. The “Step”
platform is also set to be further developed and improved in the future. Meanwhile, in order to ensure
continuous service availability and a high standard of customer service remotely, at the time and place
preferred by the customer, the availability of information and digital communication with customers is
being continuously developed. In the reporting year, on average, almost 99% of customer actions took
place in the e-environment.
The strategy of Latvenergo Group sets the overall target for the distribution segment, with the
operational targets and estimated outcomes of Sadales tīkls AS, which should be given priority in the
context of the Group’s strategic vision, subordinated to the overall target as sub-targets.

=== pdf p.30 ===
Corporate Social Responsibility
Latvenergo Group follows responsible business principles and
implements statutory and voluntary activities, contributing to sustainable
environmental, social and governance development. In its operations,
the Group implements the principles of social responsibility in
compliance with ISO 26000.
The Sustainability Policy of the Group also includes the principles and
activity criteria of corporate social responsibility (CSR). CSR activities
promote the involvement of large groups of society and ensure a
considerable long-term impact and public benefit. They are
implemented in three directions:
  • education and science development
  • cooperation with the local community
  • biodiversity
According to a corporate reputation survey conducted by TNS Latvia in
early 2026, the majority of industry experts and media representatives,
as well as almost half of the Latvian population and companies, know or
have heard about the CSR activities of the Group. 94% of the
respondents who know about the activities evaluated them positively.
81% of residents agree that Latvenergo is operating a responsible and
sustainable business.
In 2025, Latvenergo AS received Standard & Poor's Global Corporate
Sustainability Assessment, scoring 54 points. This places Latvenergo AS
among the top 30% of highest-rated companies in the Electric Utilities
sector worldwide. S&P Global recognized Latvenergo AS initiatives
across all ESG directions, including climate strategy, human capital
management, transparency and sustainability disclosure, risk
management, and business ethics.
Latvenergo Group continued to support Ukrainian society in 2025.
Several employee initiatives were organised – donations for the
purchase of drones and spare parts, as well as external batteries for
mobile devices for the defenders of Ukraine. Within 100 Cars for Ukraine
project, the Group's volunteer employees continued the transportation
of cars to Ukraine's defenders. In the reporting year, several
Latvenergo AS donations were also made to support Ukrainian society:
  • 65 vehicles
  • 120 computer monitors
  • up to 20 tonnes of transformer oil for the restoration of Ukraine's
    electricity supply system
  • solar panels and inverters, solar panel mounts and DC cable kits to
    restore and stabilise the electricity supply system of Ukraine
  • social support project competition – summer camps for children
    from Ukraine

Governance Bodies
The corporate governance of Latvenergo Group is organised and           Latvenergo AS governance bodies
implemented in compliance with governance best practice, the
regulatory framework, and corporate governance guidelines. The
principles and procedures of corporate governance are enshrined
in the Corporate Governance Policy of the Group, which has been
approved and is supervised by the Supervisory Board of
Latvenergo AS. The Management Boards are responsible for
implementing the policy at the capital companies of the Group. The
corporate governance principles of the Group are published on the
Latvenergo website.
In accordance with the requirements of the Financial Instrument
Market Law and the Law on Governance of Capital Shares of a
Public Person and Capital Companies, Latvenergo AS prepares a
corporate governance report annually. The report for 2025 was
drawn up based on the assessment of the capital company’s
compliance with the Corporate Governance Code published by the
Corporate Governance Advisory Board established by the Ministry
of Justice at the end of 2025. In 2025, all the principles set out in
the code were complied with in material respects, except for the
criterion of representation of both genders on the Supervisory
Board of the company. The report is available on the Latvenergo
website and the Nasdaq Baltic website.
A corporate governance report is also prepared by Sadales tīkls
AS. In 2025, all the principles set out in the Code were complied
with in material respects. The report is available on the
Sadales tīkls AS website.

  Audit Committee Report
  The Audit Committee of Latvenergo AS operates under the
  Commercial Law and Financial Instrument Market Law of the
  Republic of Latvia and the Rules of the Audit Committee
  approved by the Shareholder.
  No restrictions have been imposed on the actions of the
  Committee, and representatives of Latvenergo AS have
  ensured the availability of necessary information. Based on its
  work, the Audit Committee informs the Supervisory Board of
  its conclusions and recommendations.
  In 2025, in addition to its principal duties, the Audit
  Committee 19:
    • supported improvements in governance and risk
      management practices of the Group
    • evaluated the human resource development programme
      and succession planning activities
    • approved permitted non-audit services
    • discussed further improvements in sustainability reporting
      practice
    • discussed and analysed the most important events and
      trends in the energy sector and their impact on the Group’s
      activities
    • proposed changes to its regulations that were amended
      and approved by the Shareholder Meeting on
      17 September 2025
  Having assessed the information received from the Internal
  Audit Director, Compliance Control Manager, Risk Manager,
  Investor Relations and Sustainability Manager, external auditor
  and other assurance providers, nothing has come to our
  attention that would lead us to believe that the internal controls
  of Latvenergo AS are not operating adequately for the purpose
  of preparing the Annual Report 2025.

  We are submitting our activity report and assessments to the
  Supervisory Board of Latvenergo AS in April 2026.

               Svens Dinsdorfs, Chairman of the Audit Committee
                         Ilvija Grūba, Member of the Audit Committee
                Torben Pedersen, Member of the Audit Committee
                    Gundars Ruža, Member of the Audit Committee
                         Toms Siliņš, Member of the Audit Committee

Group Management
Latvenergo Group’s management model is based on corporate governance best practice. To ensure            Organisational structure of Latvenergo Group (31 December 2025)
effective Group governance, decision-making and the achievement of goals, strategic and operational
management are separate.
The Group’s strategic management is implemented by the Management Board, whose accountability
is joint according to the Commercial Law of the Republic of Latvia, and operational management is
ensured by Chief Officers, whose accountability is individual. The main duty of the Management Board
is to lead the Group to reach the objectives set in the strategy. At a minimum, the Management Board
reports to the Supervisory Board on a quarterly basis and to the Shareholder on an annual basis. Chief
Officers ensure the operational management of Latvenergo AS, including the achievement of goals
and policy implementation; they also ensure their division’s cooperation with the functions of other
divisions and the adoption of decisions in compliance with the Group’s strategy and delegation. The
divisions have been established in accordance with the strategic goals of the Group.
Considering their previous experience and knowledge of the Group’s operations, the duties of Chief
Officers are performed by the Members of the Management Board of Latvenergo AS.
At the time of the report’s publication, the duties of the Chief Officers are divided as follows:
 • Mārtiņš Čakste – Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
 • Guntars Baļčūns – Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
 • Ilvija Boreiko – Chief Development Officer (CDO)
 • Dmitrijs Juskovecs – Chief Commercial Officer (CCO)
 • Harijs Teteris – Chief Operating Officer (COO)
A certain group of administrative functions is supervised by the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO)
Arnis Kurgs, who is not a Member of the Management Board.

Changes in the organisational structure
At the end of 2024, Elektrum Next SIA commenced its work to focus activities and resources within
Latvenergo Group on the development of new green energy projects and electricity generation from
renewable energy sources, by consolidating the RES projects implemented by Latvenergo Group in
recent years. During the reporting year, Krāslavas SES SIA was merged into Elektrum Next SIA, and
Elektrum Next LT UAB was established to consolidate RES assets located in Lithuania. In 2025, the
wind farm Pienava Wind SIA was acquired.

Risk management
The objective of the Group’s risk management is to identify
significant risks in a timely manner and manage them to ensure the
achievement of the strategic goals and minimise potential losses
or harm to its reputation. Risk management is integrated into
strategy development and implementation as well as operational
activities. The Risk Management Policy of the Group sets out both
the basic principles of risk management and the responsibilities of
the parties involved in the risk management process. In
accordance with the Risk Management Policy of the Group, the
Management Boards of Group companies are responsible for
managing the risks of Group companies. The Management Board
of Latvenergo AS reports on the risk management of the Group to
the Supervisory Board of Latvenergo AS, which is responsible for
overseeing the operations of the Group’s risk management system,
at least once per year.
Significant risks are analysed in internal working groups and in the
Risk Management Committee of the Group, which is a specially
established institution on the level of the Management Board.
Within the analysis, the probability and impact of a risk is evaluated,
and an appropriate strategy for handling the risk is selected.
Any risks identified are conveyed to the internal audit system, thus
allowing the risk assessment to be used for planning the activities
of the Internal Audit. Every month, the Supervisory Board of
Latvenergo AS receives information on the risk appetite of the
Group, key risk indicators and material incidents.
In 2025, the Risk Management Regulations were refined, including
a more detailed explanation of how to assess the sustainability
aspect in the risk identification process, as well as changes to the
risk register system, allowing identified risks to be linked with
identified opportunities 28. Sustainability risks are not listed as a
separate category in the risk register system. Instead, risks can be
marked as sustainability-related, allowing them to be filtered in the
system as needed 29.
In the reporting year, the update of the Environmental and Climate
Risk Assessment methodology was initiated. The methodology
approval and risk reassessment are planned for 2026. For more
information on climate risks, see E1 Climate Change.

Baltic balancing capacity market
On February 9, 2025, Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania successfully synchronized their electricity systems
with Continental Europe. This milestone also marked the launch of the Baltic balancing capacity market,
operated by the Baltic transmission system operators. Latvenergo AS has qualified the Daugava HPPs’
and CHPPs’ units for providing balancing services and participates in the provision of these services.

=== pdf p.64 ===
Events After the Reporting Year
After the end of the reporting year, the military situation in Iran has significantly escalated, causing
disruptions to global energy supply chains, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz region. This increases
supply risks and contributes to rising energy prices. As of the report’s date of approval, these
circumstances have not had a material negative impact on the operations of Latvenergo Group and
the Parent Company. However, persistently higher energy prices are expected to increase production
costs, while weakening demand in external markets may adversely affect the Baltic region’s
economic growth prospects and create inflationary pressure. Further indirect effects will largely
depend on unpredictable developments, such as potential military escalation and the responses it
may trigger, the scale and duration of which remain uncertain.
On 10 March 2026, amendments were adopted to Cabinet of Ministers Regulation No. 432,
introducing changes to the funding allocated to Sadales tīkls AS under the European Union Recovery
and Resilience Facility. The funding has been increased by EUR 6.68 million, bringing the total
allocation to EUR 67 million. The additional funds will be invested in the REPowerEU programme
activity Development of the Electricity Distribution System Grid, including the construction of an
additional 40 km of cable lines.
On April 25, 2026, Gundars Ruža stepped down from his positions as Member of the Supervisory
Board of Latvenergo AS and Member of the Audit Committee of Latvenergo AS. The Supervisory
Board of Latvenergo AS will continue operating with four members until a new Supervisory Board
member is appointed through the selection process.
There have been no other significant events since the last day of the reporting year that would
materially affect the audited financial statements of Latvenergo Group and Latvenergo AS for the
year ended 31 December 2025.




Profit Distribution
According to the Law “On state budget for 2026 and budgetary framework for 2026, 2027 and 2028”
the expected amount of dividends to be paid by Latvenergo AS for the use of state capital in 2026
(for the reporting year 2025) amounts to EUR 141.0 million, corporate income tax calculated and paid
in accordance with the laws and regulations. The distribution of net profit and amount of dividends
payable is subject to a resolution of the Latvenergo AS Shareholders Meeting.

As a result of the double materiality assessment, the material IROs were identified, which reflect the
framework for the sustainable operations of Latvenergo Group.
The management of IROs is integrated into the operating processes of the Group’s companies, and
the supervision of these issues is addressed within the framework of fulfilling and monitoring strategies
and operational plans. The Management Boards of the Group’s capital companies handle the
implementation of strategies and policies. Twice a year, the Management Board of Latvenergo AS
assesses the progress of implementing the Sustainability Strategy (including the targets set). The
determination of Latvenergo Group’s material sustainability targets is based on internationally
recognised standards, industry guidelines and examples of best practice, as well as the strategic
objectives of the Group and impacts specific to its operations. The setting of targets and their            Broader use of renewable energy sources in the future

4.30. High-efficiency co-generation of heat and power from
fossil gaseous fuels
Latvenergo Group operates high-efficiency cogeneration (CHP)
units fuelled by fossil gaseous fuels, supplying both electricity and
heat to customers, primarily in district heating systems. These
units improve overall fuel efficiency compared to separate heat
and power production and contribute to reduced emissions at
system level.
Despite their high efficiency, cogeneration from fossil gaseous
fuels does not meet the EU Taxonomy technical screening criteria
for substantial contribution under Activity 4.30. The use of fossil
fuels prevents classification as Taxonomy-aligned, even where
efficiency thresholds are achieved.
The CHP installations are operated in compliance with applicable
EU and national environmental legislation and are subject to
permits issued by the State Environmental Service, which include
enforceable emission limit values and operational conditions.
The assets continue to play a role in ensuring security of heat
supply and system flexibility, but until a transition to renewable or
low-carbon gaseous fuels becomes technically and economically
feasible, activity 4.30 is classified as EU Taxonomy not aligned.

4.31. Production of heat from fossil gaseous fuels in an efficient
district heating and cooling system
Latvenergo Group supplies heat generated from fossil gaseous
fuels within efficient district heating systems, as defined by
Directive 2012/27/EU. As such, the activity falls within the scope of
an EU Taxonomy-eligible economic activity under Activity 4.31.
However, heat production from fossil gaseous fuels does not meet
the EU Taxonomy technical screening criteria for alignment under
Activity 4.31, notwithstanding the efficiency of the district heating
system. Accordingly, Activity 4.31 is assessed as as EU Taxonomy
eligible but not aligned.
Heat production facilities are operated under valid environmental
permits and in compliance with applicable national and EU
requirements for emissions and environmental protection. These
assets remain necessary to ensure continuity and security of heat
supply, particularly during periods of high demand or limited
availability of renewable heat sources.

CapEx
The EU Taxonomy KPI on CapEx has the same definition as Capital
expenditure in Latvenergo Group Consolidated and Latvenergo AS
Financial Statements. The proportion of CapEx for each Taxonomy
activity is calculated as the share of CapEx attributable to the
respective Taxonomy activity relative to Latvenergo’s total CapEx
in 2025. CAapEx attributable to Taxonomy-eligible and
Taxonomy-aligned activities within total CapEx is determined
through a comprehensive assessment of all capital expenditure
made by the Latvenergo Group, analysed by operating segment
and at the level of individual CapEx projects.

Material impacts, risks and opportunities
Material sustainability IROs of Latvenergo Group were identified through the double materiality assessment. For information on the double materiality assessment process, including the methodology for
identifying, assessing, and determining material IROs, see Double materiality assessment in the section General Information.
Climate change adaptation
             Impact of climate change on infrastructure resilience   LT            Latvenergo Group regularly assesses the risks caused by climate change and their impact on infrastructure, planning and
                                                                                   implementing resilience standards and protection solutions for infrastructure that ensure long-term adaptation and
                                                                                   resilience. Measures to improve infrastructure resilience are integrated into its strategic plans, also including climate risk
                                                                                   assessments in the planning of new projects. The Group works with regulatory bodies and follows international guidelines
                                                                                   to ensure compliance with best practices in climate resilience.

The physical climate risk assessment is regularly updated, taking
into account internationally recognised climate change
assessment methodologies and the latest available scientific data,
including IPCC (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change)
guidelines. The assessment is updated in response to significant
changes in data or methodologies used, rather than at strictly
defined time intervals.

The Group is progressively enhancing its policies, actions, targets
and data collection processes to ensure full alignment with ESRS
requirements over time.
The credibility of the Group’s transition pathway is supported by
an independent external assessment conducted by Moody’s,
which assigned Latvenergo AS an NZ-3 score under its Net Zero
Assessment framework, confirming a high level of confidence in
the Group’s ability to achieve its climate targets and alignment with
the Paris Agreement.
As the current strategy implementation period is approaching
completion, the Group has initiated the development of its next
medium-term operational strategy. This process will ensure continued
alignment with its long-term decarbonisation trajectory and climate
objectives. The transition plan will be reassessed and further
developed within this strategic cycle, including the refinement of
decarbonisation pathways, strengthening of climate targets, and
enhanced integration with capital expenditure planning, thereby
supporting progressive alignment with ESRS E1- 1 requirements.

Given the increasing electricity consumption and distribution volumes, the Group maintains electricity
network losses at a stable level through operational and technological measures, while recognizing
that as grid load increases, the technical challenge of preventing a rise in loss intensity also increases.
However, in order to reduce their impact, the Group sets targets to limit electricity losses and to
increase the share of certified renewable electricity in its own consumption.
Indirect Scope 3 emissions, which occur outside the Group’s direct operational control, are more
complex to measure accurately and to influence directly. No targets have been set for reducing total
absolute and specific Scope 3 emissions; however, the Group has defined measures to mitigate these
emissions, including the gradual reduction of emissions from electricity retail activities and the
promotion of customers’ selection of renewable electricity. A detailed description of the alignment
between the targets and the objectives set out in the policies is provided in the section Policies.
Results achieved in 2025:
 • direct (Scope 1) emissions fell by 17% compared to 2021 during the reporting year. The specific
   emissions rate was 0.100 tonnes of CO2 per megawatt-hour (MWh) of electricity generated
 • electricity generated from RES accounted for 66% of the total electricity output
 • the share of electric vehicles in Latvenergo Group's fleet increased to 15.6%
 • the share of certified electricity in the Group's total consumption was 80%
 • electricity distribution losses amounted to 3.66%
 • emissions from electricity retail trade increased by 8% compared to 2022. Although the share of
   green electricity chosen by customers in 2025 remained similar to that in 2022, the 2025 emission
   factor for uncertified electricity was significantly higher than in 2022. Consequently, each kilowatt-
   hour of uncertified electricity sold generated more emissions than in the 2022 reporting period
 • 12% of retail electricity clients chose green energy
The GHG emissions reduction target indicators were developed with consideration of the EU Green
Deal goals and the 2021–2030 Latvian National Energy and Climate Plan into account. The target
indicators were set based on the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) Net Zero Emissions by 2050
scenario and the energy sector decarbonisation roadmap. To ensure that the targets are aligned with
the actual emissions situation, an initial assessment of the Group’s GHG emissions inventory data was
carried out during the target-setting process, analysing the emissions structure, the main emission
sources, and historical trends. Based on this assessment, the targets were defined, ensuring
consistency with the GHG emissions inventory boundaries, methodology, and underlying data.
In 2024, Latvenergo AS received an NZ-3 score from Moody’s, which analyses the compliance of the
Group’s climate transition strategy and goals with global efforts to limit warming to 1.5 °C. The Moody’s
assessment is science-based, as it follows internationally accepted IPCC climate science findings and
scenarios. The methodology used by Moody’s integrates the latest IPCC climate models, permissible
emissions calculations and sector decarbonisation trajectories, ensuring that the rating represents the
most up-to-date scientific knowledge on climate change. Moody’s assesses not only the
ambitiousness of the goals but also their consistency with science-based decarbonisation strategies and
realistic implementation opportunities, enabling a science-based approach to evaluating climate goals.
The target indicators were set with consideration of future development factors, including anticipated
changes in sales, shifts in consumer habits and needs, regulatory requirements, and planned
technological solutions.
For information on plans to introduce new technologies and their role in achieving GHG emissions
reduction targets, see the sections Transition plan and Group Strategy.

=== pdf p.129 ===
In 2024–2025, Latvenergo AS completed the remediation of historical pollution at CHPP-2 by cleaning
the regenerative air heater section, where technological deposits had accumulated from earlier fuel‑oil
operations. The project included the removal and disposal of 2,486 tonnes of hazardous waste,
approximately 85% of which was recycled. The works were carried out through close cooperation
between internal structural units, significantly reducing future pollution risks within the CHPP-2 site.
Although at Group level quantitative emission reduction targets have been set only for air pollution, the
management of all types of emissions, including emissions to air and water, within the Group is ensured
in compliance with the requirements defined in environmental permits, the limit values established in
applicable legislation, and through the implementation of object-specific technical solutions. This
approach is aimed at preventing pollution at its source and avoiding significant environmental harm,
with a focus on improving process efficiency, ensuring control of pollutant concentrations, preventing
leakage and accident risks, and continuously enhancing monitoring and operational control systems.
To monitor and control pollution, the Group maintains an extensive network of monitoring systems, including:
  • automatic emission measurement systems at production plants
  • wastewater quality control systems
  • a groundwater quality monitoring network
Regular funding is provided for the maintenance and upgrading of these systems, which includes both
technical maintenance and personnel training.
Implementing these measures contributes to achieving the objectives of Latvenergo Group’s pollution
management policy, ensuring their integration into the Group’s strategic planning and day-to-day
operations. The development of RES capacities and the modernization of existing generation assets
directly support the policy objective of reducing air pollution and GHG emissions, while also mitigating
pollution risks throughout the entire asset life cycle. Investments in the reconstruction of HPPs and in
electricity distribution infrastructure contribute to pollution prevention and control by reducing the
likelihood of hazardous substance releases and improving energy efficiency. In addition, cooperation
with supply chain partners and end users ensures that pollution management requirements are applied
beyond the Group’s direct operations, thereby strengthening the achievement of policy objectives
across upstream and downstream value chains.

In the event that a pollution risk is identified, the Group assesses
the need for remediation of the respective site by determining the
extent of pollution, selecting appropriate solutions, and planning
the associated costs, while also evaluating the broader impact on
the environment and society and implementing appropriate
measures where necessary.
In the short term, the expected financial impact is relatively limited
and is primarily related to the investments required to maintain and
upgrade emission control systems. The activities currently
implemented by the Group in the area of pollution prevention and
control and the operation of its production facilities comply with
the applicable BAT guidelines and the threshold values determined.
In the medium term, the Group foresees the need to continue
investing in the modernisation of production processes, which may
require a moderate level of financial resources. In the longer term,
however, it is expected that regulatory changes, technological
developments and market requirements may require moderate to
significant investments to ensure the transition to environmentally
friendly technologies. At the same time, such investments may also
generate positive financial impacts in the long term by reducing
future risks and potential costs.

                                                                          The Group implements well-defined policies at several levels:
 • the Biodiversity Transition Plan for 2026–2028 defines the
   Group's approach to integrating biodiversity into energy
   transition processes, emphasising the interrelationship
   between climate change and biodiversity, and covers the
   Group’s own operations and the most important upstream and
   downstream part of the value chain. The plan is based on the
   impact mitigation hierarchy and provides timely impact
   assessments within the development of new RES projects,
   targeted measures to improve biotopes and habitats in existing
   production assets, and the use of energy infrastructure for
   nature restoration and public education initiatives. It aims at
   managing the impact on biodiversity in a structured manner,
   ensuring alignment with climate and sustainability objectives
   and promoting resilient, nature-inclusive development of the
   energy sector

E4-4

Targets
The targets of the Group are closely linked to its impact on biodiversity and ecosystems, as well as to
dependencies, risks and opportunities identified along the value chain. With respect to biodiversity
and ecosystem matters, the Group’s strategy does not establish baseline values or base years; instead,
it defines specific, achievable targets for the coming years. Progress towards the targets’ achievement
is primarily assessed against the predefined target values rather than in comparison to historical
baselines. This approach was chosen as it aligns more effectively with the Group’s strategy. No interim
targets have been established. For information on stakeholder involvement in the target-setting process
of the strategy, please refer to the section General Information. The targets are set voluntarily and:
 • reflect the Group’s commitment to reducing negative impact on ecosystems and have been
   developed to monitor and assess how the Group's activities affect the natural environment
 • help manage the Group’s reliance on ecosystem nature's services and fosters the development of
   sustainable practices to ensure the long-term conservation of natural resources
 • serve as a tool for risk management by identifying environmental challenges and promoting investment
   in environmental restoration and reduction of emissions; at the same time, they open up new
   opportunities, such as the development of green technologies, promotion of environmentally friendly
   solutions and strengthening of cooperation with stakeholders in the area of sustainable development
In general, the targets serve as a strategic tool that helps integrate biodiversity considerations into the
decision-making processes of the company, thus strengthening its sustainability along the value chain.
The targets include both quantitative objectives with defined achievement timelines and qualitative
objectives and measures that describe the Group’s strategic approach to the protection and restoration
of biodiversity and ecosystems, as well as to the management of related impacts and risks in areas
where precise quantitative indicators are not applicable. Latvenergo Group constitutes the framework
for setting the targets. The sections About the Group and Operating Segments provide information on
the geographical scope of Latvenergo Group’s economic activities and its main operational sites. The
targets mainly relate to the Group’s own operations and include some elements of the upstream and
downstream value chain. Biodiversity compensation measures have not been used in setting targets.
The setting of targets and their achievement have not been verified by an external verifier.
Latvenergo Group’s biodiversity protection measures are planned and implemented in accordance with
the internationally recognised mitigation hierarchy principle. Based on this approach, Latvenergo Group
has set four commitments in the area of biodiversity and ecosystem protection. These commitments have
been included and approved within the framework of the Sustainability Strategy of Latvenergo Group for
2024–2026, thus strengthening the Group’s long-term commitment to nature conservation.
The methodologies used in setting the goals are grounded in the Group’s long-term collaboration with
scientific institutions and experts. The target of improving the ecological quality of habitats is based
on the annual survey and monitoring data from the BIOR Institute on river ecosystem quality. The target
of enhancing the status of fish species and habitats is informed by the BIOR Institute’s 2020–2023
scientific studies on the dynamics of migratory fish populations in the Daugava River basin and the
assessment of fish migration opportunities. The target or the ratio of planted to felled trees is derived
from studies on the effectiveness of forest restoration and regulatory requirements for developing
WPPs. The methodology for assessing impacts on protected areas relies on the latest scientific
research on the dynamics and distribution of protected species populations, ensuring a scientifically
robust approach to impact assessment and the planning of protection measures.

Latvenergo Group constitutes the framework for setting the targets. The sections About the Group and
Operating Segments provide information on the geographical scope of Latvenergo Group’s economic
activities and its main operational sites. The Latvenergo Group’s resource use and circular economy
objectives primarily apply to the Group’s directly managed generation, grid and resource management
activities, while also integrating the most significant value chain aspects – the sustainable supply of
biomass, the recycling of equipment and materials, as well as cooperation with suppliers to promote
innovation and the use of local resources. The targets are set on a voluntary basis, using a
methodology that considers the current situation, the feasibility of technical and economic solutions,
the capacity of existing waste management infrastructure, and examples of best practices within the
sector. While industry guidelines and available research are taken into account, a detailed scientific
analysis has not been conducted. No interim targets have been established. For information on
stakeholder involvement in the target-setting process of the strategy, please refer to the section
General Information. Progress towards the targets' achievement is primarily assessed against the
predefined target values rather than in comparison to historical baselines. This approach was chosen
as it aligns more effectively with the Group’s strategy and allows for greater flexibility in responding to
developments within the energy sector. Progress is regularly reviewed and, if necessary, updated in
line with changes in regulatory frameworks and the development of the Group's operations.
Latvenergo Group’s commitments in the area of the circular economy and performance in the reporting year:
 • use of sustainable biomass – Liepājas enerģija SIA uses a biomass fuel – wood – at its production
   sites. Over the reporting year, 100% of biomass fuels used met the criteria for sustainability and
   saving GHG emissions, ensuring compliance with the requirements of the regulatory enactments
   of the European Union and the Republic of Latvia. Traceability of biomass is ensured throughout
   the supply chain. Biomass extraction is based on the principles of sustainable forestry, thus
   ensuring the conservation of biodiversity and reforestation
 • measures to promote sustainable consumption – Latvenergo Group implemented more than ten
   measures to promote sustainable consumption in the reporting year
   Efficient use of equipment has been ensured at the combined heat and power plants by carrying
   out regular maintenance repairs and renewing key components, consequently extending the life
   of the equipment and avoiding premature replacement.
   In the area of electricity network infrastructure, the share of the isolated and weatherproof power
   lines in 2025 reached 69% of the total volume of power lines, which is a 2% increase from 2024.
   Sadales tīkls AS implements the Technical Policy, which defines common basic principles for
   efficient maintenance and sustainable development of the distribution electricity network. In 2025,
   the level of electricity losses remained stable at 3.66%, slightly higher than the previous year.
   Recycling of dismantled materials is an important contribution to the reuse of materials. More than
   2,200 tonnes of end-of-life grid infrastructure materials were submitted for recycling in 2025.
   Furthermore, support was provided to Ukraine with 65 vehicles, 120 computer monitors, and
   materials for the restoration and stabilisation of the power supply system.
   Latvenergo Group promotes cooperation with local entrepreneurs, developing innovations, using local
   resources and reducing the environmental impact of the materials used. In the construction process of
   the Laflora Energy WPP, the Latvian branch of Nordex (Germany) provides innovative technology by
   constructing turbine towers using a hybrid design combining reinforced concrete and metal. The
   reinforced concrete tower sections are manufactured in Latvia, at the Consolis Latvia SIA factory.

 Working conditions
         The workload of employees exceeds the desired    MT    P    OO    In the reporting year, the number of overtime hours in the Group’s parent company increased by approximately 16% compared
         levels in some units                                              to 2024. In 2025, the number of overtime hours at Sadales tīkls AS decreased by 2.3% compared to 2024. An increase in the
                                                                           volume of overtime has been recorded in certain structural units and is not systematic. It is mainly related to fluctuations in the
                                                                           volume of operations, increased project intensity and limitations in resource availability. The Group identifies the increase in
                                                                           employee workload as a significant work condition risk, which may potentially affect employee well-being, work-life balance and
                                                                           the long-term sustainability of work capacity. Workload indicators are regularly monitored. Responsible managers are involved
                                                                           in situations where in-depth analysis or additional management attention is required. To remedy increased employee workload,
                                                                           the following activities are implemented: flexible work organization, supervision sessions, educational initiatives on work–life
                                                                           balance, improvements to the working environment, etc.

 Trustees                              Within the companies of the Group, trustees represent the interests of employees in occupational safety and cooperate with the units and management in order to
                                       improve the work environment. Trustees have the right to freely express their own opinions and those of employees related to the setup and implementation of the
                                       occupational safety system at the company and to receive regulatory documents, explanations and other information related to occupational safety. In 2025, Latvenergo
                                       AS and Sadales tīkls AS had 25 employee-elected trustees from the Latvian trade union Enerģija. The employer provides occupational safety training for trustees

 Channels of communication             The Group makes detailed workload plans, recording working time according to the duties and responsibilities of the employees. To reduce persistent work overload and
                                       boost the performance of employees, they are provided with a range of educational activities covering work-life balance, time management, and setting priorities. In
                                       2024, 119 employees participated in supervision sessions. 55 managers participated in the Manager Power Group development programme, and 800 employees attended
                                       various educational conferences.

 Collective bargaining agreement       See the section Collective bargaining coverage and social dialogue.

 Equality in recruitment               The recruitment process is fair and non-discriminatory. Recruitment specialists:
                                        • assess all applications based on uniform criteria
                                        • cooperate with managers and employees involved across all stages of recruitment
                                        • ensure the equal treatment of all candidates
                                        • follow the approach of non-discrimination in accordance with the Labour Law, Code of Ethics and good recruitment practices

 New jobs for the transition to the    Within the development of SPP in the reporting year, Latvenergo AS created one new workplace with the maintenance of generation equipment as the priority. Meanwhile,
 green economy                         a separate structural unit with nine positions was created for business growth and innovation development. The number of employees in the combined heat and power
                                       plants remained unchanged during the reporting year. In transitioning to more sustainable infrastructure maintenance and development solutions, Sadales tīkls AS created
                                       five new workplaces. Sadales tīkls AS implemented a Task Management System (UTG) and a Work Management System (DRPR) for digital work order processing and
                                       time tracking. With the introduction of UTG and DRPR, the organisation and execution of repair work have been optimised, work planning improved and travel to sites
                                       reduced, resulting in significant reductions in fuel consumption and CO2 emissions.

 Measures to promote the internal      Latvenergo AS Summer Festival, nominations and White Tablecloth Day events, team-building activities, the renewed Idea Bank, the summer event “CONNECTED”, as
 culture and cooperation               well as the new Microsoft 365 platform enable employees to take an active part in recognising their colleagues’ achievements and shaping the modern and engaging
                                       company culture.

 Participation in conferences          Since 2023, Latvenergo AS has made it possible for its employees to participate in online conferences and access video recordings of the conferences. In the reporting
                                       year, employees attended approximately 150 different conferences and forums to familiarise themselves with industry developments and maintain professional
                                       competence, for example, Life Balance Parts 1 and 2, Sustainability, LeadershipFactor, Subject: Creativity, Baltic Business Forum 2025: Leadership. Growth, Innovation.,
                                       Leader 2025, District Heating and Energy Technologies, Energy Sector 2025. In the reporting year, the average employee feedback rating for all conferences was 8.9
                                       (on a 10-point scale).

 Supervision                           In 2023, as part of a pilot project, customer service employees had an opportunity to try supervision as one of the most effective methods of emotional self-regulation
                                       and stress management. In 2024, supervision was offered to employees in units where the work environment risk assessment revealed high psycho-emotional risk, as
                                       well as units with the lowest ratings in the well-being dimension of the employee experience survey. In 2025, the scope of supervision participants was expanded by

                                          offering this service to managers. In 2025, 21 supervision groups were provided. 133 employees participated in group supervisions and 3 employees received individual
                                          supervisions. More than 80% of supervision participants rate them very positively or positively, as well as highly value the professionalism of the supervisors. Participants
                                          also positively assess the opportunity to view issues in a broader context, to hear experiences of their colleagues, and to acquire practical techniques for managing
                                          stress in everyday life.

 Safety training                          The Group provides occupational safety training, as well as professional upskilling training to its employees. The Group organises training in first aid, electrical safety,
                                          working at heights, working with hazardous equipment, and other specialised training to meet the needs of its employees. The Group fully covers the cost of such
                                          training, and employees can attend it during working hours.

 Performance of hazardous work            Employees from the generation and trade, and distribution business segments are engaged in performance of hazardous work related to the operation and maintenance
                                          of the generation equipment/infrastructure. Only properly trained, skilled and mandatory health checks completed employees are allowed to carry out hazardous work.
                                          Workplaces are specially prepared for the safe performance of work, including checks of the equipment and tools needed to ensure safe operation. Particular attention
                                          is paid to conducting goal-specific briefings, used to explain to employees the safety requirements of the corresponding work, the procedure for performing the work,
                                          the potential risks and their mitigation measures, and the course of action in emergencies. To ensure safe operations, individuals are appointed to supervise work
                                          performance, monitor compliance with safety requirements, and perform regular checks to prevent any breaches of the requirements set. This ensures that hazardous
                                          work is carried out safely, reducing the risk of incidents.

 Protective equipment                     Employees of the Group are provided with collective and personal protective equipment. The selection of workwear, footwear, and personal protective equipment is
                                          based on the specific nature of the work, the degree of protection required and the latest solutions available.

Customer satisfaction and loyalty index of Sadales tīkls AS
Sadales tīkls AS customer satisfaction and loyalty rose to 72 index
points in 2025 (+2 points compared to 2024), exceeding the high
indicator threshold. The growth was achieved in both the
corporate (70 points, +2 points) and household (74 points,
+3 points) segments. The particularly high rating of the large
corporate and municipalities segments (75 points, +1 point) proves
the excellent service of Sadales tīkls AS. Customer needs remain
unchanged: continuity of the electricity supply, value for money,
reputation of the company, ease of cooperation and information
(incl. data availability).

 • the target for 2025 was 60–70 index points
 • total customer satisfaction and loyalty increased to an all-time
   high of 72 index points in 2025

which defines both the basic principles of risk management and the responsibilities of employees and
management involved in the risk management process. In accordance with the Group Risk
Management Policy, the Management Boards of the Group’s capital companies are responsible for the
capital companies’ risk management. At least once a year, the Management Board of Latvenergo AS
submits a report on the Group’s risk management to the Supervisory Board of Latvenergo AS, which
is responsible for overseeing the Group’s risk management system.

         Sustainability Strategy 2024–2026 developed and         LT   A    OO     The Sustainability Strategy not only promotes sustainable and responsible progress but also improves the company’s

                                                                                  or corporate sustainability obligations, can seriously damage a company’s reputation and lead to financial sanctions.

         sustainability score in a changing environment                           the Group’s assessment as a sustainability-focused company, which can affect reputation, leading to repercussions.

                                                                                  financial flow.

         electricity generation assets                                            better fundraising opportunities.

                                                                                  greatly facilitates the provision of information to stakeholders.

Statement of Management
Responsibility
Based on the information available to the Management Board of Latvenergo AS, Latvenergo Group
consolidated financial statements and Latvenergo AS financial statements for the year ended
31 December 2025 have been prepared in accordance with IFRS accounting standards as adopted by
the EU and in all material aspects present a true and fair view of the financial position, profit and loss
and cash flows of Latvenergo Group and Latvenergo AS.
The Management Report of the Group’s Consolidated and Latvenergo AS Annual Report for 2025
provides a description of the main risks and uncertainties the Group faces. The sustainability
information included in the Management Report has been prepared in accordance with the European
Sustainability Reporting Standards defined by Sustainability Information Disclosure Law and
Article 8(4) of Regulation (EU) 2020/852 of 18 June 2020 on the establishment of a framework to
facilitate sustainable investment, and amending Regulation (EU) 2019/2088.
Information provided in the Management Report is accurate.
Latvenergo Group Consolidated and Latvenergo AS Annual Report 2025 is approved by the
Management Board of Latvenergo AS on 28 April 2026 and is signed by Member of the Management
Board Guntars Baļčūns as authorized person.




This document is signed with a secure digital signature and contains a time stamp.


Guntars Baļčūns
Member of the Management Board
of Latvenergo AS

Notes to the Financial Statements
1. Corporate Information
All shares of public limited company Latvenergo, parent company of Latvenergo Group (hereinafter – Latvenergo AS or the Parent Company) are owned by the Republic of Latvia and are held by the Ministry of
Economics of the Republic of Latvia. The registered address of the Parent Company is 12 Pulkveža Brieža Street, Riga, Latvia, LV–1230. According to the Energy Law of the Republic of Latvia, Latvenergo AS is
designated as a national economy object of State importance.
Latvenergo AS is power supply utility engaged in electricity and thermal energy generation, as well as sales of electricity and natural gas. Latvenergo AS is one of the largest corporate entities in the Baltics.
Subsidiaries included in Latvenergo Group (hereinafter – the Group), participating interest in subsidiaries, associated companies and other non-current financial investments are disclosed in Note 16.
Latvenergo AS and its subsidiaries Sadales tīkls AS and Enerģijas publiskais tirgotājs SIA are also shareholders with 48.15% interest held in company Pirmais Slēgtais Pensiju Fonds AS (Latvenergo AS holds
46.30% of interest) that manages a defined–contribution corporate pension plan in Latvia.
The Management Board of Latvenergo AS:
Since 26 January 2024 the Management Board of Latvenergo AS was comprised of the following members: Mārtiņš Čakste (Chairman of the Board), Dmitrijs Juskovecs, Guntars Baļčūns, Harijs Teteris and
Ilvija Boreiko.
The Supervisory Board of Latvenergo AS:
Since 9 April 2025 the Supervisory Board of Latvenergo AS was comprised of the following members: Aigars Laizāns (re-elected as Chairman on 25 April 2025), Kaspars Rokens (re-elected as Deputy Chairman
on 25 April 2025), Toms Siliņš, Rodžers Jānis Grigulis and Gundars Ruža (until 25 April 2026).
Since 1 March 2024 till 8 April 2025 the Supervisory Board of Latvenergo AS was comprised of the following members: Aigars Laizāns (Chairman since 8 March 2024), Kaspars Rokens (Deputy Chairman),
Toms Siliņš and Gundars Ruža (until 25 April 2026).
The Audit Committee of Latvenergo AS:
